name: quic-go-e937eb8f-blind30
instr:
# quic-go-regen

An application built on this library dials a peer, brings a link up, moves data over it, gives up on a transfer partway, and winds itself down, and it now gets all of that wrong in ways that look unrelated to one another. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the callers changed. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Getting a link up at all is the first thing to go. Almost every fetch against a locally launched peer dies during setup with the identity credential refused: the throwaway credential minted on the fly for the loopback address no longer covers what the dialing side checks. The disposable signing authority such a credential chains up to is separately minted with a validity span beginning a year later than it used to, so links relying on that chain fail rather than completing. A peer that has to pick the hostname the dialer asked for out of the dialer's opening greeting takes the list of names from an offset before the position it computed rather than after it, so the greeting is misparsed and the link either never comes up or comes up under the wrong identity. A peer announcing exactly the largest permitted count of simultaneous two-way transfers is now turned away while its opening limits are being taken in, although one announcing one less is still accepted.
